current.text: He is coming back from a torn ACL. His rehab was reported as going well and he was expected to be ready for opening night.
At Rockets media day he made troubling comments about his knee and said he does not feel like himself.
He is a projected starter at point guard. If he has a setback, Marcus Smart would start in his place.
The Rockets are expected to limit his minutes early. Lloyd projects about 32 minutes a night: near 30 at the start, rising to 34 or 35 by the end of the season.
He is expected to sit some back-to-backs early in the season and to miss other games too. Bad shooting stretches are also expected.
The Rockets have only 14 back-to-backs this season.
The Houston guard rotation is crowded with Amen Thompson, Marcus Smart, Bogdan Bogdanovic and Reed Sheppard.
With many other ball handlers on the team, Lloyd does not expect high assist numbers from him.
With our March 28 end date, the Rockets play a weak 3-3-4 schedule in the fantasy playoffs, 10 games over three weeks.
Experts agree his ESPN rank of 74 is far too high. Lloyd ranks him 120 to 135 in category leagues and sees him as a late point guard flyer.

durable.text: He tore his ACL and missed the whole 2025-26 season.
He is a poor shooter from the field, especially on two-point shots, and he hurts FG%. His three-point shooting is good.
He gives good steals and assists with relatively low scoring.
He takes good care of the ball and keeps his turnovers low.
He is at an advanced age for a player returning from an ACL injury.

note: Lloyd ranks him 120 to 135. That is far below ESPN's rank of 74 (5 USD value) and close to Yahoo's rank of 153 (1 USD), so treat him as a 1 to 2 USD late guard and not a mid-round buy. He fits punt FG% builds best, where his threes, assists, steals and low turnovers count and his 39% shooting does not. Early in the season, check his minutes (expected near 30 at first), how many back-to-backs he sits, and his knee. Also keep in mind that Houston plays only 10 games in our playoff weeks.
